papers.title_en: Impacts of generative AI skill development on academic adaptation and learning outcomes among university students
papers.evidence: 大学生生成式AI技能发展与学习成效研究
papers.tldr: 大学生生成式AI技能如何随时间发展、又如何影响学业适应与学习结果仍不清楚。研究以313份回溯问卷和18名学生访谈，结合描述比较、探索性结构方程与主题分析。结果发现技能轨迹异质（快速提升后平台期34.2%、稳步提升28.4%、延迟加速21.1%），评估AI输出提升较难，作业是最常见驱动。技能成长可通过作业流程适应间接关联学业收益，但轨迹组间差异在多重校正后不明显。
papers.abstract_en: Understanding how university students perceive the development of their generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) skills over time can clarify how GenAI use relates to learning and academic outcomes. This study examined perceived skill-development trajectories, changes in learning practices, and associated academic gains using a retrospective questionnaire with 313 analyzed responses and interviews with 18 students across subject areas. Descriptive and comparative analyses and exploratory structural equation modeling (SEM) were integrated with thematic analysis. Perceived developmental trajectories were heterogeneous: 34.2% of students reported rapid early improvement followed by a plateau, 28.4% steady improvement, and 21.1% delayed acceleration. Development was also uneven across skills, with improvement in evaluating GenAI outputs perceived as more challenging; assignments were the most frequently selected driver of skill growth. Interviews further indicated increasingly specific prompting, tailored verification, and selective delegation, although some students reported stable routines, dependence, skipped reasoning, or improvements attributable partly to better GenAI tools. Academic gains were reported more often for assignments than for examinations. The SEM indicated a positive indirect association between perceived skill growth and academic gains through adaptation of assignment processes, whereas academic gains did not clearly differ across developmental trajectory groups after multiplicity correction. The findings suggest that perceived GenAI skill development varies in both trajectory and skill domain and is associated with changes in learning practices and differentiated academic benefits.

papers.title_en: DagFlow AI: Agentic Synthetic Data Generation for Personalized Statistics Learning
papers.authors: David Arthur, Ranjini Grove, Zaher Kmail, Curtis Atkisson
papers.evidence: 智能体AI为统计学习生成个性化数据集
papers.tldr: 在数据分析课程中，教师需要同时匹配学生兴趣、学习目标和技能水平的数据集，但这类数据集往往难以找到。DagFlow-AI 是一个 agentic 数据生成工具，它不直接模仿现有数据或逐条生成观测，而是借助大语言模型的推理能力，指定透明、可复现的数据生成机制组件，再由程序按机制生成观测。该工具可构建贴近真实情境的合成数据集，并与 GAISE 指南及 PPDAC 教学框架对齐，为个性化统计学习提供可定制的数据支持。
papers.abstract_en: To provide personalized learning experiences in courses that teach data analysis skills, instructors often search for datasets that appeal to a student's interests, align with specific learning objectives, and are appropriate for the student's skill level. Datasets that match all three criteria can be difficult to find. DagFlow-AI is an agentic AI data generation tool that creates realistic, synthetic datasets tailored to these criteria. Rather than mimicking existing datasets or generating observations directly, DagFlow-AI uses the broad knowledge and reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs) to specify the components of transparent, reproducible data-generating mechanisms from which observations are generated programmatically. We illustrate how the tool can be used to construct a realistic, synthetic dataset and describe how it aligns with both the Guidelines for Assessment and Instruction of Statistics Education (GAISE) and the Problem, Plan, Data, Analysis, and Conclusion (PPDAC) framework for teaching data analysis

papers.title_en: TutorCaseBench: A Case-Grounded Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Tutors in Supporting Students with Challenging Behaviors
papers.authors: Yeon Su Park, Chanyoung Park, Tae Soo Kim, Seungju Kim, Hyunwoo Kim, Daho Jung, Jinsung Yoon, Juho Kim
papers.evidence: 面向LLM智能导师教学支持能力的评估基准
papers.tldr: 大语言模型正被广泛用作 AI 导师，但现有评测忽视了学习与行为困难学生常见的挑战性行为。作者提出 TutorCaseBench，将教育学、教育心理学和特殊教育的质性案例研究转化为具体情境、师生对话与基于原始证据的评分量表。基准覆盖五类挑战，共 923 段对话，并设置开放式回答（1560 题）与多项选择（2537 题）两种评测。11 个先进模型中最强模型在开放式情形下仅满足 55.8% 的评分标准，且更擅长识别策略而非生成贴合情境的回应，揭示干预识别与情境适配之间的差距。
papers.abstract_en: LLMs are increasingly used as AI tutors, yet existing benchmarks overlook the challenging behaviors common among students with learning and behavioral difficulties. We introduce TutorCaseBench, a benchmark that grounds AI-tutor evaluation in qualitative case studies from pedagogy, educational psychology, and special education. Our pipeline converts documented student categories into case-specific scenarios, tutor-student dialogues, and rubrics grounded in source evidence. The benchmark contains 923 dialogues across five challenge types, evaluated through open-ended response generation (1,560 items) and multiple-choice selection (2,537 items). Across 11 state-of-the-art LLMs, even the strongest model satisfies a rubric criterion in only 55.8% of open-ended cases, while models are better at selecting appropriate strategies than generating situated responses. These results reveal a gap between intervention recognition and context-specific adaptation, especially for open-weight models. All data are publicly available at https://github.com/kixlab/TutorCaseBench.

papers.title_en: Algorithmic drift in generative adaptive learning
papers.authors: Firuz Kamalov, Hana Sulieman, Ahmed El Sayed, Sivaraj R., Nitesh Sughnani
papers.evidence: 生成式自适应个性化辅导系统中的算法漂移
papers.tldr: 生成式AI有望普及个性化辅导，但自适应系统的长期稳定性缺乏理论。本文把算法漂移形式化为学习者与导师耦合的动力系统，并用蒙特卡洛模拟验证：由在线追踪器或LSTM知识追踪网络驱动IRT课程策略。作者提出时间公平稳定器TFS，定期重测学习者能力。模拟中TFS能缩小成绩差距，而通用探索不能。
papers.abstract_en: Generative artificial intelligence promises to democratize personalized tutoring, yet the longitudinal stability of adaptive systems remains under-theorized. Current ethical discourse focuses on static bias. This paper argues that a distinct threat lies in algorithmic drift: a feedback loop in which minor, demographically asymmetric observation errors compound over time into systemic inequities. We make three contributions. First, we formalize algorithmic drift as a coupled learner--tutor dynamical system. Second, we corroborate this theory with an agent-based Monte Carlo simulation in which either a transparent online tracker or an LSTM deep-knowledge-tracing network drives an IRT-based curriculum policy. Third, we introduce the temporal fairness stabilizer (TFS), a targeted intervention that periodically re-probes learner capability, and benchmark it against standard exploration baselines with explicit group-fairness metrics and replication-level inference. Within the modeled environment, TFS closes the achievement gap where generic exploration does not, and we characterize the conditions under which it succeeds. We separate what is established analytically, what is demonstrated in simulation, and what remains to be validated with real learners. Our results reframe algorithmic fairness in education as a temporal property of a closed loop rather than a deployment-time checkbox.

papers.title_en: Supporting or Replacing Students' Reasoning? Cognitive Offloading in AI-Assisted Proof Learning
papers.authors: Eason Chen, Sophia Judicke, Kayla Beigh, Xinyi Tang, Isabel Wang, Nina Yuan, Zimo Xiao, Chuangji Li, Shizhuo Li, Reed Luttmer, Shreya Singh, Maria Yampolsky, Naman Parikh, Yvonne Zhao, Meiyi Chen, Scarlett Huang, Anishka Mohanty, Gregory Johnson, John Mackey, Jionghao Lin, Ken Koedinger
papers.evidence: AI聊天机器人辅助本科证明学习与认知卸载
papers.tldr: 研究关注AI聊天机器人是否会让学生把推理论证“外包”给AI，从而损害数学证明学习。作者在本科证明数学课中对153名学生做错峰开放随机实验，对比聊天机器人与需先提交证明再获反馈的作业界面。结果显示，早期使用AI的学生作业分高2.56分，但考试成绩无显著差异；全面开放后，每多发送100条聊天消息，后续考试低3.02分，且低自我效能感经由更多聊天使用间接拉低成绩。作业反馈界面则无此负面关联，提示AI辅导设计需嵌入课程活动而非开放聊天。
papers.abstract_en: We studied 153 students in an undergraduate proof-based mathematics course with staggered-access to an AI support system. Students were randomly assigned to receive an AI chatbot and a homework-feedback interface earlier or later in the course. During the period when only the early-access group had access, their homework scores were 2.56 points higher, but exam performance did not differ significantly between groups, suggesting that improved AI-supported homework performance did not translate into detectable gains on a subsequent exam. After all students received access, every additional 100 messages sent to the AI chatbot was associated with a 3.02-point lower score on the subsequent exam. A mediation analysis showed a significant indirect association linking lower baseline self-efficacy to greater chatbot use and, in turn, lower exam scores: a one-point decrease in self-efficacy corresponded to 0.62 fewer exam points through chatbot use. These findings raise concerns that students may use the chatbot to offload their cognitive reasoning. Use of the homework-feedback interface, which required students to submit their proof attempts before receiving feedback, was not negatively associated with exam performance. We recommend against using a chatbot for AI tutoring and suggest exploring a tutor embedded in the course activities.

papers.title_en: Measuring undergraduate students' reliance on generative AI during problem-solving: Scale development and validation
papers.authors: Chenyu Hou, Gaoxia Zhu, Vidya Sudarshan, Fun Siong Lim, Yew Soon Ong
papers.evidence: 测量本科生在问题解决中对生成式AI的依赖
papers.tldr: 现有AI依赖测量多绑定决策结果，难以适用于结果非二元或非即时明确的复杂问题解决任务。本研究面向本科生开发生成式AI使用行为量表，收集问题解决活动后的问卷并进行探索性与验证性因子分析。结果识别出反思性使用、谨慎使用、轻率使用和协作使用四个因子，总量表内部信度良好，并在两类任务中验证模型拟合可接受。该量表为评估人机协作问题解决中的AI依赖行为提供了有效工具。
papers.abstract_en: Reliance on AI describes the behavioral patterns of when and how individuals depend on AI suggestions, and appropriate reliance patterns are necessary to achieve effective human-AI collaboration. Traditional measures often link reliance to decision-making outcomes, which may not be suitable for complex problem-solving tasks where outcomes are not binary (i.e., correct or incorrect) or immediately clear. Therefore, this study aims to develop a scale to measure undergraduate students' behaviors of using Generative AI during problem-solving tasks without directly linking them to specific outcomes. We conducted an exploratory factor analysis on 800 responses collected after students finished one problem-solving activity, which revealed four distinct factors: reflective use, cautious use, thoughtless use, and collaborative use. The overall scale has reached sufficient internal reliability (Cronbach's alpha = .84). Two confirmatory factor analyses (CFAs) were conducted to validate the factors using the remaining 730 responses from this activity and 1,173 responses from another problem-solving activity. CFA indices showed adequate model fit for data from both problem-solving tasks, suggesting that the scale can be applied to various human-AI problem-solving tasks. This study offers a validated scale to measure students' reliance behaviors in different human-AI problem-solving activities and provides implications for educators to responsively integrate Generative AI in higher education.

papers.title_en: TESSA: A Governance-Oriented Custom GPT for SME Guidance under the EU AI Act: Design, Implementation, and Evaluation
papers.authors: Chalisa Veesommai Sillberga, Kai-Kristian Kemella, Pekka Sillberga, Katri Harjuveteläinenb, Mika Saaria, Pekka Abrahamssona
papers.evidence: 面向AI治理教育的定制GPT教育工具
papers.tldr: 生成式AI普及使中小企业面临EU AI Act合规与治理挑战。研究以设计科学研究开发治理导向的Custom GPT教育工件TESSA，并用100个基准场景对比基线ChatGPT。结果显示治理对齐率初步为90%对83%、专家复核为71%对70%，且TESSA重复执行一致性较高。贡献包括治理导向工件、人工验证的法规更新机制和多维评估框架。
papers.abstract_en: The increasing adoption of generative AI presents new opportunities while raising AI governance and regulatory challenges, particularly for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) navigating the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act (EU AI Act). To support AI governance education, this study developed TESSA, a governance-oriented educational artifact within the OpenAI Custom GPT environment. Following a design science research approach, TESSA was evaluated against baseline ChatGPT using 100 benchmark scenarios through governance alignment assessment, human expert review, and consistency testing. Preliminary LLM-assisted assessment showed governance alignment rates of 90% for TESSA and 83% for baseline ChatGPT, while independent validation by an AI regulation law practitioner yielded 71% and 70%, respectively. Human expert review indicated that both systems provided generally strong governance guidance, while TESSA maintained high consistency across repeated executions. The findings suggest that governance-oriented grounding can support structured, practical, and stable AI-assisted compliance guidance for SMEs. The study contributes (i) a governance-oriented Custom GPT artifact for AI governance education, (ii) a human-validated regulatory update mechanism, and (iii) a multidimensional evaluation framework for governance-oriented AI artifact.
